title: Music Beneath the Radio Calls
tests: Tests whether added music remains audibly subordinate to the original speech, with intelligibility preserved throughout the delivered video.

faults.what: The landscape source footage has been changed to a tightly cropped portrait presentation, removing substantial cockpit and surrounding scenery despite the instruction not to change the footage.
The output includes subtitle overlays, an unrequested visual change in an audio-only editing task.

judge.summary: The seven-second output includes the transcribed key radio line but visibly reframes the footage and adds subtitles, while the music and its balance cannot be verified.

must_haves.item: The output preserves all seven seconds of the original cockpit footage without visual changes or extra shots.
must_haves.why: The output is seven seconds long, but its portrait crop differs substantially from the landscape source, and subtitle overlays are visible.

must_haves.item: A tense instrumental music bed is audible, with no added singing.
must_haves.why: The supplied sound information gives a peak level and speech transcription but does not describe music, mood, or singing.

must_haves.item: The original radio calls remain present and synchronized, including the clearly intelligible line 'Rook, you with me?'
must_haves.why: The transcription confirms that 'Rook, you with me?' is heard, but it does not establish preservation and synchronization of all original calls; the visible reply subtitle is not proof of audible speech.

must_haves.item: During every spoken line, the music is perceptibly below the voice and does not mask words with loud beats, swells, or accents.
must_haves.why: A transcription and overall peak of -2 dB do not establish relative voice/music levels or masking throughout the clip.

must_haves.item: The music is not simply muted for the entire clip; it is audible while remaining subordinate to speech.
must_haves.why: No supplied audio description confirms that music is audible or subordinate to speech.
